comments.note: MovieEditorView.axaml: The PrimaryAction (Save & Exit) and SecondaryActions (Discard) buttons placed in PageHeaderView's slots use compiled bindings (x:DataType=MovieEditorViewModel). However, PageHeaderView sets DataContext=this in its constructor, so these buttons' DataContext at runtime will be the PageHeaderView instance, not MovieEditorViewModel. The compiled bindings will silently fail, rendering these header buttons non-functional. The bottom toolbar buttons remain functional. QA should verify at runtime and consider either: (a) using $parent binding syntax, (b) using a relay ViewModel pattern, or (c) adding a DataContext reset in PageHeaderView's ContentPresenter template.

summary: Code review FAIL. Two blocking issues found. (1) BackCommand={Binding CloseCommand} in MovieEditorView.axaml likely fails at runtime: PageHeaderView sets DataContext=this in its constructor, overriding the inherited DataContext. Avalonia compiled bindings on an element use that element's own DataContext as source. Since PageHeaderView.DataContext=PageHeaderView (not MovieEditorViewModel), CloseCommand is not found, BackCommand remains null, and the Back button is ENABLED even when HasChanges=true — AC 2 fails at runtime. (2) PrimaryAction/SecondaryActions buttons in the header are confirmed non-functional dead UI (QA bug, Developer flagged as known issue) — both commands silently fail due to the same DataContext issue. The bottom toolbar has working duplicates. Fix: remove PrimaryAction/SecondaryActions content; set BackCommand imperatively in code-behind.

comments.note: BLOCKING — BackCommand binding likely fails at runtime. MovieEditorView.axaml declares BackCommand="{Binding CloseCommand}" on the PageHeaderView element. PageHeaderView's constructor sets DataContext=this before InitializeComponent(). In Avalonia, compiled attribute bindings on an element use that element's own DataContext as the binding source. Since PageHeaderView.DataContext=PageHeaderView (not MovieEditorViewModel), the binding {Binding CloseCommand} looks for CloseCommand on PageHeaderView and fails silently, leaving BackCommand=null. With null BackCommand: (1) the Back button has no command, so it is ENABLED (not disabled) even when HasChanges=true — AC 2 fails at runtime. (2) The breadcrumb click guard (if BackCommand is not null && ...) is also bypassed — user can navigate away with unsaved changes via breadcrumb. FIX: Set BackCommand in code-behind after DataContext is set. In MovieEditorView.axaml, add x:Name='PageHeader' to the PageHeaderView element. In MovieEditorView.axaml.cs, bind it imperatively: DataContextChanged += (_, _) => { if (DataContext is MovieEditorViewModel vm) PageHeader.BackCommand = vm.CloseCommand; }. Alternatively, write a headless AvaloniaFact test that instantiates MovieEditorView with a MovieEditorViewModel DataContext and verifies PageHeader.BackCommand is not null and that the back button IsEnabled is false when vm.HasChanges=true.

BLOCKING — PrimaryAction and SecondaryActions slots contain dead non-functional UI. The 'Save & Exit' Button (Command={Binding SaveAndExitCommand}) and 'Discard' Button (Command={Binding DiscardChangesCommand}) are declared as content of PageHeaderView.PrimaryAction and SecondaryActions. These buttons are rendered inside PageHeaderView's ContentPresenter, whose DataContext inherits from PageHeaderView (DataContext=this). SaveAndExitCommand and DiscardChangesCommand don't exist on PageHeaderView, so both compiled bindings silently fail. Both buttons render visible but do nothing when clicked. The bottom toolbar (row 1) has functional duplicates of both buttons. FIX: Remove the PrimaryAction and SecondaryActions content entirely from MovieEditorView.axaml. The bottom toolbar is the canonical action surface. No AC requires header action buttons.

Architectural note: PageHeaderView.DataContext=this is correct for its own internal AXAML bindings (BreadcrumbItems, IsBackVisible, Title, BackCommand rendered internally). However, it means parent AXAML cannot set PageHeaderView's styled properties (BackCommand, PrimaryAction, SecondaryActions) via {Binding} attribute syntax — only literal values or code-behind assignment work. The PrimaryAction/SecondaryActions styled properties are therefore only usable via code-behind or {x:Static} references. This should be documented in the PageHeaderView API as a constraint.

[documentation-forward] PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: Document the DataContext=this constraint on the PageHeaderView public API. Callers cannot set styled properties (BackCommand, PrimaryAction, SecondaryActions) via {Binding} AXAML attribute syntax from a parent view — only literal values or code-behind assignment are reliable. This prevents subtle silent binding failures in future views.
